title: homelab-stack.json
description: A stack's manifest, version 9: what the stack asks of the host. Each route, path, egress, port, GPU, containers and API entry is a grant the operator approves. The host's Check is the authority; this schema is for the editor.

name.description: The stack's suggested name: 1-32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and '-', starting with a letter. The operator picks the installed name.

nixpkgs.description: The nixpkgs the stack is built with: nixos-unstable, nixos-YY.MM or a 40-character NixOS/nixpkgs commit.

icon.description: The stack's icon on the dashboard.

services.description: The stack's services as the dashboard shows them, each by its unit inside the stack.

added_folders.description: How the dashboard asks for the folders the operator adds to the stack: each has a name and is mounted at <under>/<name>. A hint, not a grant.

under.description: The directory in the stack the named folders are mounted in, such as /shares.

label.description: What the stack calls the folders, as a heading: one line of at most 40 bytes, such as Shares.

description.description: What the stack does with them, for the dashboard.

read_only.description: Whether a new folder starts read-only. The operator may change it.

routes.description: Hostnames the host's Caddy serves over HTTPS, each to a port in the stack.

variables.description: Values the host gives the stack: env, secret, path or address.

egress.description: Destinations beyond the default. The stack reaches the internet and the host's Caddy on 443 without one; the LAN, other host ports, Tailscale and IPv6 are blocked unless opened here.

ports.description: Ports on the host forwarded into the stack, for protocols Caddy cannot carry (RTSP, a game server, a media server's direct connections).

gpu.description: The host's GPU devices and drivers in the stack.

containers.description: Podman may run in the stack (it needs system calls a container refuses by default).

api.description: The homelab daemon's API scopes the stack may call with its token: read (every GET) and control (start, stop and restart units).

health.description: What makes a new version healthy. Every unit must be active and the HTTP probe must answer 2xx, or an update is rolled back.

units.description: Every service that must be up, such as nginx.service.

http.description: A probe on the stack's own address.

path.description: Starts with / and has no spaces.

backup.description: What the stack recommends backing up. Nothing is backed up until the operator adds a folder to a backup.

prepare.description: A oneshot unit in the stack (a database dump) started and waited for before the folders are copied.

icon.description: An https URL, a file in the stack's repo (.svg, .png or .webp, at most 256 KiB, such as icons/app.svg), or a name in the dashboard-icons set (such as jellyfin).

unit.description: The service's unit inside the stack, such as plex.service.

host.description: A label such as photos, served privately as photos.<the host's domain>, or a full hostname.

port.description: The port in the stack the service listens on (on 0.0.0.0).

max_body.description: Caddy's request body limit, such as 500MB or 50GB. Leave out for the default.

name.description: 1-64 characters of A-Z, 0-9 and '_', starting with a letter. HOMELAB_API_TOKEN, HOMELAB_API_URL, HOMELAB_DOMAIN and HOMELAB_DASHBOARD_URL are the host's.

kind.description: env: a plain value. secret: write-only. path: a host folder bound in at mount. address: IPv4 addresses or CIDRs (and the words lan, vpn and tailnet, which the operator may tick), used by egress and ports as $NAME.

description.description: One short sentence: what the value is, with an example where it helps. The dashboard shows it as the variable's help.

required.description: The stack does not build until the operator gives a value.

default.description: path only: the host folder used while the operator has picked none.

mount.description: path only: where the folder appears inside the stack, an absolute path used once.

read_only.description: path only: bind the folder read-only.

type.description: env only: what the value is, for the dashboard's input.

owner.description: path only: a user the module declares, which takes the host folder's uid.

group.description: path only: a group the module declares, which takes the host folder's gid.

to.description: host (the host itself; its mail relay is port 25), an IPv4 CIDR such as 10.0.0.5/32, or $NAME for an address variable.

port.description: The port on the host. Never 22, 53, 80 or 443.

from.description: The clients allowed: lan (the host's LAN), IPv4 CIDRs, or $NAME for an address variable.

label.description: What the folder holds, as the backup page shows it.

path.description: A folder inside the stack, such as /var/lib/app. Not /.

variable.description: A path variable whose host folder is backed up.

exclude.description: Patterns left out, each with why.
